content: 【大纪元2026年11月16日讯】11月12日，是孙中山先生一百六十周年诞辰。北京高规格举行纪念大会。习近平在讲话中声称，中国共产党人是孙中山先生革命事业“最坚定的支持者、最忠诚的合作者、最忠实的继承者”，并强调孙中山坚定维护国家统一。 在我看来，习近平给中共戴上孙中山“最忠实的继承者”这顶桂冠，纯属对历史的无耻篡改。 思想体系：三民主义与共产主义 南辕北辙 孙中山毕生奋斗的思想旗帜，是民族、民权、民生三民主义。民族主义追求的是推翻帝制、建立独立的民族国家；民权主义的核心，是“主权在民”，要建立一个有宪法、有国会、有选举、有言论自由的共和政体；民生主义主张平均地权、节制资本，是在私有制和市场经济的框架内追求社会公平。孙中山晚年虽然提出“联俄容共”，但他接纳的，是苏俄的援助与合作，而非马克思主义的国家学说。 共产主义则是一套完全不同的理论与实践：阶级斗争、无产阶级专政、消灭私有制、党的绝对领导。这套学说恰恰是孙中山民权主义所要防止的东西。孙中山在《三民主义》演讲中反复告诫：民权不是从天而降的恩赐，而是要靠制度来保障的。他设想的五权宪法、国民大会、地方自治，无一不是以限制权力、还政于民为出发点。以阶级专政取代主权在民，以一党永久执政取代宪政共和，这与三民主义在根本处是对立的。习近平说二者是“继承”关系，在思想史上是站不住脚的。 历史进程：继承者，还是终结者？ 看历史事实，更能说明问题。 辛亥革命之后，中国曾有过民初的国会选举、多党竞争与新闻自由，虽然幼稚、混乱，却是共和的萌芽。1927年之后国共分道，1949年中共建政，中国走上了一条与孙中山宪政蓝图完全不同的道路。反右、大跃进、文革，国家权力不受任何制约，公民权利荡然无存——孙中山毕生追求的“民权”，在这段历史中不是被继承，而是被悬置乃至终结了。 有人说，中共完成了国家统一与工业化，这是对孙中山遗志的继承。但孙中山的遗志从来不只是“富国强兵”，更是“还政于民”。《建国方略》里铁路港口的蓝图可以实现，宪政的蓝图却恰恰是至今没有兑现的那一部分。只继承建设蓝图，不继承权力制衡的设计，这叫选择性继承，谈不上“最忠实”。 两岸问题的叙事也值得注意。孙中山逝世时，中华民国已经存在，今天台湾地区继承的，正是当年那部宪法和五院体制的余绪。北京以“孙中山维护国家统一”来论证统一主张，却回避了一个更基本的问题：孙中山主张的统一，是在共和宪政框架内的统一，而不是以专政消灭共和的统一。 为什么偏偏是孙中山？ 那么，为什么中共如此执著地宣称自己是孙中山的传人？ 原因不难理解。 第一，孙中山是两岸与海内外华人最大公约数的政治符号，谁掌握了对他的解释权，谁就占据了正统叙事的制高点。 第二，中共的合法性叙事需要一条从辛亥到今天的历史主线——把1949年说成辛亥革命的“完成”，就能把百年历史写成一个连续的、必然的剧本。 第三，“继承者”的说法，能把孙中山宪政理想中那些至今未兑现的承诺，收编进自己的话语体系，使其失去独立的批判力量。 但符号的借用，代替不了思想的检验。判断“继承”与否，标准不应是纪念大会的规格，而应看基本理念是否相续、制度设计是否相承、历史走向是否相合。以此衡量，三民主义与共产主义、宪政与专政、主权在民与党的领导，处处相悖，何谈“最忠实”？ 孙中山留给中国的最宝贵遗产，不是某一项工程蓝图，早日而是他的信念：中国应当成为一个主权在民的现代共和国。真正纪念孙中山，最好的方式不是把他的名字写进纪念讲话，更不是给自己带上“最忠实的继承者”的桂冠，而是实现他的遗愿，早日把中国建成一个真正的民主宪政国家。恰恰在这个最根本的问题上，中共建政后的所作所为，无一不是在开历史的倒车，与孙中山的遗愿背道而驰，有如此厚这种颜无耻的“最忠实的继承者”吗？

title: The Reluctant Winner of the AI Race
zh_title: 人工智能竞赛的勉强获胜者
summary: 过去几周，人工智能行业比以往任何时候都更接近金融灾难。投资者已经开始对为人工智能建设提供资金的巨额循环支出提出更多问题。主要的人工智能数据中心参与者正在背负越来越多的债务，其中一些以垃圾债券的形式存在。在中期选举中，美国人以压倒性多数投票支持了会减缓数据中心发展的公投和候选人。然后，似乎这还不够不确定，黄仁勋上周承认与一名所谓的中国间谍有染，并辞去了首席执行官的职务。
content:
过去几周，人工智能行业比以往任何时候都更接近金融灾难。投资者已经开始对为人工智能建设提供资金的巨额循环支出提出更多问题。主要的人工智能数据中心参与者正在背负越来越多的债务，其中一些以垃圾债券的形式存在。在中期选举中，美国人以压倒性多数投票支持了会减缓数据中心发展的公投和候选人。然后，似乎这还不够不确定，黄仁勋上周承认与一名所谓的中国间谍有染，并辞去了英伟达首席执行官的职务。英伟达是人工智能芯片制造巨头，一直是人工智能繁荣的财务后盾。据报道，甚至在黄仁勋辞职带来不确定性之前，英伟达就在考虑限制部分支出承诺。换句话说，如果这是一个泡沫，那么现在就是泡沫破灭的时候了。 [阅读：] 价值 5.7 万亿美元的 Face-Plant 然而，明天，在这种巨大的不确定性中，Anthropic 将继续进行大规模的公开发行——开始在证券交易所交易，并计划在此过程中筹集超过 900 亿美元，这将是有史以来最多的 IPO。这个时机要么是灾难性的，要么是一场政变。需求火爆：据报道，该公司收到的订单数量几乎是可用股票数量的七倍。 Anthropic 可能不仅成为世界上最大的公司之一，而且成为人工智能行业最新的救世主和关键人物。
然而，对于我们其他方面的经济福祉来说，这不一定是好消息。明天的公开募股将为该公司令人震惊的 12 个月画上句号。多年来，Anthropic 一直被称为 OpenAI 的安全先锋弟弟。该公司由达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 和其他六名前 OpenAI 员工于 2021 年创立，一直在其老兄弟的阴影下运营，后者已成为人工智能行业的代言人。去年 11 月，Anthropic 发布了新模型 Claude Opus 4.5，情况发生了变化。该模型被广泛认为代表了人工智能能力的阶跃变化，帮助迎来了代理人工智能时代，并将 Anthropic 推向了领先地位。该公司的许多核心早期赌注——对人工智能编码和其他工作场所工具的重视，以及安全和责任第一的定位——都得到了回报。 OpenAI 专注于聊天机器人和 TikTok 风格的人工智能视频应用程序等消费产品，而 Anthropic 则吸引了大型企业客户。根据其 IPO 文件，自 2025 年底以来，Anthropic 的季度收入增长了八倍多。仅今年 7 月至 9 月，该公司的盈利就超过 160 亿美元。即使在一年前，如果你告诉任何分析师 Anthropic 将在 OpenAI 之前上市，他们也会感到震惊。现在看来很明显了。 （Anthropic 没有回应置评请求。）如果 Anthropic 的公开发行顺利进行，它将重新燃起对整个行业的信心和投资，或许还能解决其不稳定问题。
Anthropic 在股票市场上市（“ANT”，如果你好奇的话）可以被视为成熟的标志——这证明 Anthropic 和人工智能作为经济的主要力量将继续存在。它预计其支出（将流经数据中心和人工智能生态系统的资金）将同步增长。 Anthropic 致力于在数据中心和相关基础设施上支出超过 9000 亿美元，并在其 IPO 文件中表示，预计其支出将

【原文 English Original】
Over the past few weeks, the AI industry has teetered closer to financial calamity than ever. Investors have begun asking more questions about tremendous and circular spending that is funding the AI build-out. Major AI data-center players are loading up on more and more debt, some of it in the form of junk bonds. In the midterm elections, Americans overwhelmingly voted for referendums and candidates that would slow data-center development. And then, as if that weren’t enough uncertainty, Jensen Huang admitted last week to having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy and stepped down as CEO of Nvidia—the AI-chipmaking giant that has been the financial backstop for the AI boom. Even before the uncertainty produced by Huang’s resignation, Nvidia was reportedly considering curbing some of its spending commitments. In other words, if this is a bubble, about now would be the time for it to pop. [ Read: ] A $5.7 Trillion Face-Plant And yet, tomorrow, amid this tremendous uncertainty, Anthropic will forge ahead with its immense public offering—beginning to trade on stock exchanges and aiming to raise more than $90 billion in the process, which would be the most of any IPO ever. The timing could either be calamitous or turn out to be a coup. Demand is red-hot: The company reportedly received nearly seven times more orders than there are shares available. Anthropic may emerge not just as one of the world’s largest companies but as the AI trade’s latest savior and lynchpin. That’s not, however, necessarily good news for the rest of our economic well-being. Tomorrow’s public offering will cap off an astounding 12 months for the company. For years, Anthropic was known as OpenAI’s safety-forward younger sibling. Formed by Dario Amodei and six other former OpenAI employees in 2021, the company consistently operated in the shadow of its older sibling, which became the face of the AI industry. That changed last November, when Anthropic released a new model, Claude Opus 4.5. The model was widely considered to represent a step change in AI capabilities, helped usher in the era of agentic AI, and pushed Anthropic to the front of the pack. Many of the company’s core, early bets—its emphasis on AI coding and other workplace tools, its positioning as being safety- and responsibility-first—paid off. While OpenAI focused on consumer products such as a chatbot and a TikTok-style AI-video app, Anthropic attracted big enterprise customers. Anthropic’s quarterly revenues, according to its IPO filings, have grown more than eightfold since the end of 2025. Just from July to September of this year, the company made more than $16 billion. If, even a year ago, you’d told any analyst that Anthropic would go public before OpenAI, they’d be shocked. Now it seems obvious. (Anthropic did not respond to a request for comment.) If Anthropic’s public offering goes well, it will fuel renewed confidence and investment in the industry as a whole and, perhaps, fix its wobble. Anthropic’s listing on stock markets (“ANT,” if you’re curious) can be taken as a sign of maturation—evidence that Anthropic and AI, as a major force in the economy, are here to stay. Not only is the company’s revenue growth meteoric; it expects its spending—money that will flow throughout the data-center and AI ecosystem—to grow in lockstep. Anthropic is committed to spending more than $900 billion on data centers and related infrastructure, and said in its IPO paperwork that it expects its expenditures to only “increase significantly.” Being bullish on Anthropic means, by necessity, being bullish on AI; it means believing that, at some point, all of this spending pays off, yielding, as Anthropic states in its founders’ letter, cures for cancer and Alzheimer’s disease, alongside tens of trillions of dollars in global economic growth. Any number of investors looking to sell shares of Nvidia could switch that money over to Anthropic, and Amodei could assume the role of Jensen Huang: the steadfast and responsible shepherd of the industry. Of course, the opposite could happen. Should Anthropic’s offering flop, it will almost certainly kick off an extended period of pain for Silicon Valley. Anthropic’s demand for more and more computing power—to train more powerful models and serve more customers—is perhaps the single most important indicator of the strength of the data-center boom. If investors prove nervous about even this company, which is cleanly winning the AI-capabilities race and growing its revenues at a historic pace, then the entire edifice is suspect. And a successful IPO, in and of itself, would reflect good vibes but not directly change the underlying mismatch between revenues and planned spending across the AI industry, Anthropic included. Another $900 billion in promised AI and data-center expenditures may not make this infrastructure boom more sustainable—but it could add to losses if and when the bubble does pop. Perhaps the most likely course is somewhere in between total AI dominance and collapse. Anthropic goes public and sees sustained, even spectacular, success as a business and a stock. The AI-investment flywheel , flush with new cash, spins ever faster. Fortune 500 companies that deploy Claude agents see their profit margins rise. Meanwhile: All of the AI money flooding markets, alongside spending on data-center construction, keeps inflation high. All of those agents mean that the labor force remains stagnant, or shrinks. If you listen to Anthropic’s communications, both the IPO and the company’s immediate profits are secondary concerns. The company’s prospectus warns investors, again and again, that it might make decisions that do not maximize profits. And that significant increase in spending, Anthropic notes, “may increase regardless of whether our financial performance improves.” That cavalier attitude toward making money is in line with Anthropic’s origins as a safety-oriented AI lab (and it was, at the start, genuinely a lab). It’s also in line with Anthropic leadership’s zealotry about the inevitability and imminence of superintelligence, which stands out even among their AI-executive peers. Going public, and all of the capital that allows Anthropic to access, is a sign that the firm is intent in securing its role in dictating the direction of such all-powerful machines. This IPO lands at a time of anxiety about AI as the technology of the future. Rogue-agent swarms and a deluge of AI-powered cyberattacks have left many wondering whether the industry should slow down and led many to suggest that it do so—including Amodei himself . And yet, Anthropic is forging ahead, shutting down fear and criticism just as all of its peers have done at every turn; the AI industry’s self-styled superego may turn out to be the id. Anthropic was founded, above all, on faith in Amodei’s clairvoyance and judgment. Seemingly the Anthropic CEO’s most candid answer to why he’d left OpenAI was in a Bloomberg interview this past summer in which he said, “Why argue with someone when you don’t have the same vision and you don’t trust them? The way to resolve it is: You go off and do your thing; they go off and do their thing.” Going public is entirely consistent with such messianism. What sets Anthropic apart is that it is a company of true believers—in the almost transcendental power of AI and, as important, in themselves. Last year, at Anthropic’s headquarters, I had a telling conversation with two of its researchers, Trenton Bricken and Sholto Douglas. Bricken was telling me that in an ideal world, he’d want AI development to proceed far more slowly and carefully. Douglas disagreed: Any delay “comes at the cost of millions of lives,” he told me. At the time, I wrote that the impulses to speed and slow AI development seemed to be at war within the company. Now one side has clearly won out.

title: 秦伟平参加德州农工大学MVP国际交流会议：关注科技创新与下一代教育发展
summary: 纵览中国报道 2026年11月16日至17日，首届美台MVP（Most Valuable Partnership，最有价值伙伴）学术交流会议在美国德克萨斯州农工大学（Texas A&M University）举行。来自学术界、公共政策、科技产业及国际事务领域的专家学者和专业人士齐聚一堂，围绕国际关系、科技创新、半导体产业、人工智能、经济合作及人才培养等议题展开交流。 美国海军退伍军人、联邦雇员、经济学者及作家秦伟平（Weiping “George” Qin）参加了此次会议。秦
content: 纵览中国报道 2026年11月16日至17日，首届美台MVP（Most Valuable Partnership，最有价值伙伴）学术交流会议在美国德克萨斯州农工大学（Texas A&M University）举行。来自学术界、公共政策、科技产业及国际事务领域的专家学者和专业人士齐聚一堂，围绕国际关系、科技创新、半导体产业、人工智能、经济合作及人才培养等议题展开交流。 美国海军退伍军人、联邦雇员、经济学者及作家秦伟平（Weiping “George” Qin）参加了此次会议。秦伟平目前正在Golden Gate University攻读公共管理硕士（MPA），同时也是德州Katy ISD学区董事会第六席位候选人。 聚焦科技创新、经济合作与人才培养 本次会议由德州农工大学Bush公共服务学院（Bush School of Government & Public Service）下属的Scowcroft国际事务研究所，与台湾大学社会科学学院合作举办，是双方持续推动学术交流与机构合作的一项重要活动。 会议为期两天，议题涵盖美国与台湾的国际合作、印太地区发展、科技政策、半导体产业、人工智能以及经济和公共政策领域面临的共同挑战。 随着人工智能和半导体技术持续发展，科技创新与人才培养已经成为全球经济和教育领域的重要议题。会议不仅安排了专家学者的专题讨论，也为来自大学、政府、研究机构和产业界的参与者提供了交流机会。 会议期间还安排了文化交流活动，让与会者在学术讨论之外进一步了解不同文化背景和社会环境。 秦伟平与林佳龙部长会面 会议期间，秦伟平有机会与台湾外交部长林佳龙部长见面交流。 秦伟平此前曾在社交媒体X上与林佳龙部长互动并相互关注，因此这次能够在德州农工大学现场见面，他表示倍感亲切。 秦伟平在个人社交媒体上分享了现场照片，并对林佳龙部长的主题演讲给予积极评价。他认为，演讲内容具有启发性，而林部长亲切、随和的交流风格也给他留下了深刻印象。 对于秦伟平而言，这次会议不仅是一次了解国际事务和科技发展趋势的机会，也让他进一步认识到，不同文化、专业和教育背景的人士之间开展交流，有助于拓展视野、分享经验，并为未来合作创造更多可能性。 从国际交流思考Katy ISD教育的未来 值得关注的是，秦伟平将此次国际交流活动与自己参与地方教育公共事务的经历联系起来。 作为三个孩子的父亲，他的家庭与Katy ISD学区有着直接联系。作为Katy ISD董事会第六席位候选人，他也持续关注学区教育质量、校园安全、教师支持、财政管理和信息透明度等问题。 在会后分享中，秦伟平表示，虽然此次会议讨论的主要是国际事务、科技和经济合作，但其中许多理念同样适用于地方教育。 在一个日益互联的世界里，学生需要的不仅是课堂上的基础知识，还包括批判性思维、沟通能力、创新意识、跨文化理解，以及与不同背景的人合作的能力。 他特别强调，科学、技术、工程和数学（STEM）教育对于学生未来的发展越来越重要。学校应当帮助学生接触新知识、新技术和不同的思维方式，让他们有机会了解现实世界中的问题，并学习通过创新与合作寻找解决方案。 秦伟平希望，未来Katy ISD能够继续探索更多有意义的教育交流与合作机会，进一步丰富STEM学习、科技创新和拓展学生视野的活动，为学生提供更加多元的学习体验。 多元文化是社区的优势，教育应帮助学生面向未来 Katy是休斯顿地区具有多元文化背景的社区之一，许多家庭拥有不同的语言、文化和专业经历。 秦伟平认为，这种多元性是社区的重要优势。学校不仅承担传授知识的责任，也可以帮助学生学会理解不同观点、尊重文化差异，并在合作中建立信心。 他同时指出，国际交流不能取代优质教育的基本条件。认真负责的教师、积极支持孩子的家庭、安全的校园环境，以及对公共教育资金的合理管理，始终是学校发展的基础。国际教育交流和合作应当成为这些基础工作的有益补充，为学生创造更多接触新知识、拓展视野和了解世界的机会。 在他看来，地方教育与国际交流虽然处于不同层面，但最终都指向一个共同目标：让下一代拥有更好的教育条件，以及面对未来机遇和挑战的能力。 从公共服务经历到地方教育参与 秦伟平曾在美国海军服役，之后从事联邦政府相关工作，并拥有工商管理硕士（MBA）学位。目前，他正在Golden Gate University攻读公共管理硕士（MPA），进一步学习公共政策、政府管理和公共服务。 近期，他还参加了Katy ISD董事会工作研究会议，就学区预算修订、建设项目合同及公共资金使用透明度等事项发表意见。他认为，公共教育资源应当得到审慎管理，每一笔公共支出都应当有清晰的用途和合理的价值，并最终服务于学生和教师。 这些经历也构成了他参与学区董事会竞选的背景。 秦伟平计划竞选2027年5月Katy ISD Board of Trustees Position 6。他提出的教育主张涵盖学生学业成绩、学生支持、教师队伍建设、财政责任以及信息透明和公众信任等方面。 从参加国际学术交流会议，到关注地方学区预算和教育政策，秦伟平希望将公共服务、教育管理和社区参与结合起来，推动学校更加重视学生的长远发展。 本次MVP会议为来自不同领域的参与者提供了交流平台，也让秦伟平有机会从国际科技与教育发展的角度，进一步思考地方学校如何帮助学生做好未来准备。 正如他在会后分享中所表达的理念： 不同的视角，共同的机遇，为孩子们创造更美好的未来。 了解秦伟平的教育理念与社区愿景： https://weipingqintx.com Weiping “George” Qin（秦伟平） Katy ISD Board of Trustees Position 6 候选人 Served Our Country. Defending Our Classrooms.

content: 看到一則新聞，想弄清楚事情的來龍去脈；朋友傳來一個聳動的說法，不確定是真是假；某個議題討論了好幾天，想知道大家究竟在爭論什麼⋯⋯以前我們會去Google一下，現在你會打開搜尋引擎，還是直接問 AI？ 數年前，我們在討論的是社群媒體的崛起：大家從主動打開新聞網站，轉向在社群平台上接觸新聞；那媒體該如何跟上這個變化，吸引用戶進來自己的門戶？一但AI出現後，連這個問題也被淘汰了，因為把新聞貼給 AI，就能請它解釋背景、整理不同立場，看不懂的地方，還可以請 AI 用簡單的方式說明。「零點擊搜尋」早已是常態，媒體甚至難以追求讓讀者點進來讀。 科技帶來的改變，不只是接收資訊的管道。AI 整理好的回答，也可能讓我們不再點開原始報導，也未必知道答案裡的資訊，是誰採訪、查證和寫下的。那麼，未來專業的新聞機構到底還有甚麼角色？我們還需要記者和編輯做哪些事？ 今年，端傳媒在年度用戶調研裡，邀請大家一起思索這個假想：如果有一天，AI 已經能準確回答任何議題的任何問題，而且不再出錯，專業新聞機構還需要存在嗎？ 結果是，幾乎所有人都說：需要。近 99% 填問卷的人表示，專業的新聞機構仍需存在。 那麼，大家期待新聞機構做些什麼？ 期待到現場發現問題，也在事件過後持續追問 即使假設 AI 能準確回答問題，差不多每兩個填問卷的人，就有一個認為，值得追問的問題、需要記錄的事件，還是得靠專業媒體人到現場、持續追問。這是最多人的選擇，其次才是採編理念、操守與責任，以及個性化回應以外的新視角。 你有過這樣的經驗嗎？當一件事發生時，接連讀了好幾篇新聞，過一陣子想知道後來怎麼了，卻找不到後續。 近半填問卷的人，就遇到了類似的情況。信任的媒體雖然報導了自己關心的議題，卻零零散散、不夠持續；也有人幾乎找不到相關報導，只好自己東拼西湊。 香港的獨立書店，是端一直追蹤的議題。從2016年銅鑼灣書店事件，到近年獨立書店被搜查、結束營業，同樣是書店新聞，每一次採訪面對的處境卻不一樣。 搜查之後，書店還能繼續營業嗎，結束結束營業後，經營者又去了哪裡？新聞熱度退去，這些問題未必已經有了答案。 「追蹤長期議題」也是許多人閱讀端的原因。一則留言寫道：「當傳統媒體在某個社會事件的現場完全絕跡的時候，希望端仍然可以給出一定的調查與報道。」 另一位則直言：「多去现场吧，我不想再看文献综述了。」 面對真假未明的消息，將近一半的人先找信任的媒體確認 聽到一則真假未明的聳動消息時，讀者真的會先問AI嗎？我們發現，將近一半填問卷的人，會先看看信任的媒體有沒有報導；如果沒有，就暫時當作還沒確認。有人會在感興趣時自己找一手來源，也有人簡單搜尋一下，再問 AI。 重大事件發生時，不少人也會主動找端。在社群蓬勃發展的現在，當消息一則接一則，說法五花八門，這時大家最想知道的，往往是哪些事已經確認、哪些還不能下結論。 這是今天大家面對消息的方式。這也是約三成填問卷的人，仍把採編理念、操守與責任，列為新聞機構需要存在的首要理由。 讀一篇報導，可以知道它訪問了誰、用了什麼資料，也知道哪些問題還沒查清楚。如果後來發現有錯，還能找到更正，以及更正的原因。答案之外，這些交代也影響我們願不願意相信新聞的真實性。 而確認消息是真的之後，下一個問題往往才剛開始：它為什麼會發生？ 比起知道發生什麼，大家更想理解為什麼 十個填問卷的人裡，有八個以上追蹤新聞，是為了弄懂事情為什麼發生、背後是什麼樣的結構，比想知道「究竟發生了什麼」的人更多。也有人想確認有人認真看待這件事，或希望重要的事被記錄下來、不被遺忘。 香港大埔宏福苑火災發生時，最先要報導的是火災新聞。但隨著消息傳來，更多疑問也接著出現：火為什麼燒得這麼大？救援困難在哪裡？居民經歷了什麼？ 大火當天，端立刻派出記者到達火災現場，並在翌日清晨立刻發出一篇詡實深度解讀。隔天開始，端陸續透過深度內容解釋火勢與救援的問題，並繼續留守現場再寫報道救援情況。 火勢熄滅，居民的生活不會立刻回到原本的樣子。到了2026年，獨立委員會舉行聽證會，端持續整理重點，也回頭記錄居民災後的生活。 從當天的火災，到後來的聽證會，報導追問大火如何發生，也記錄人們如何度過大火之後的日子。 火災發生後，我們立刻刊出深度文章，解讀當時最重要的多個疑問：高樓救火為何困難？屋苑圍標是否火災成因之一？這些「複雜事件的脈絡」的報道，被許多人列為端很難被取代的價值。同樣受歡迎的內容形式也包括系列報導、評論和解讀類文章。 跨地域視角是端最難取代的價值 打開端，大家想讀的未必是同一件事。在這次調研裡，住在中國大陸和香港的人，最希望端持續追蹤當地的政治與社會；住在台灣的人，則最想看國際時事。 而當目光落在同一則新聞上，討論也未必朝著同一個方向。 今年7月，香港一名獨立書店店員被警方帶走，身上穿著一件黑色 T 恤，上面印著「我是書店店員」。照片傳到台灣，這幾個字也出現在演唱會的螢幕上。 有香港人感謝台灣的支持，也有人看到自己的處境成了舞台背景，覺得被消費。 端在報導中問：香港的書店正在經歷什麼？台灣的書店經營者，又怎麼看待這場聲援？為何台港兩地互相關心，卻似乎喪失了對話的基礎？ 這樣的跨地域視角，是這次調研中最多人看重的端的價值。超過六成填問卷的人，認為它難以由其他來源取代。 在離散時代，我們更需要這種跨地域視角：搬到新的地方，怎麼認識所處的社會，又怎麼看待原來的家？「異鄉人」是這次調研中最多人喜愛的欄目，也有不少人期待端開設「離散華人社群」新欄目，繼續寫下移動之後的生活。 一位讀者在留言裡說：「走出自己的同溫層，不要再用舊視角去理解這個快速變化的世界。」 面對AI，大家也期待新聞機構說清楚使用的界線 你可能已經會請AI整理新聞，但如果打開一篇報導，內容也是AI寫的，感受會一樣嗎？ 問卷最後的開放題裡，有人直接說：「不要放棄純人手產出。要看AI的話我們自己生成就行。」 也有人期待端試試新工具：「探索AI對媒體的幫助與界線，讓新科技幫助端的理念。」 另有人在意文字讀起來的感受：「希望能够跟所谓的AI味内容区分开来。希望读到有情感、真诚的文字。」 這些留言不能代表所有人的態度，但能看見，大家在意的不只是工具好不好用，也包括打開端時，想讀到什麼。 對 AI 的關注，同樣出現在對新欄目的期待裡。「AI 鑑識與事實查核」的新欄目得到超過四成填問卷的人支持。當 AI 也開始產生我們每天接觸的資訊，怎麼辨認、如何查核，又成了新的閱讀需求。 支持獨立新聞，讓重要的事有人繼續追問 問卷從一個假設開始：如果 AI 已經能準確回答任何問題，新聞機構還需要存在嗎？ 這份用戶調研告訴我們：讀者還是希望有人去現場，追蹤還沒有結束的事。在AI年代，更需要有人查證、交代依據，為報導負責。 這份期待，也反映在大家如何看待訂閱。將近一半的人，把「支持獨立新聞事業」當成成為端會員最重要的意義，其次是「為一項服務付費」。 一位讀者在留言牆寫下：「作為離散的香港人，支持專業媒體是能力所及的小事。今日新聞就是明天的歷史，為下一代留住真相。」 從一家書店的去留，到一場大火之後的生活，還有許多故事沒有結束。訂閱是為值得讀的內容付費，也支持記者再次回到現場，把後來的事繼續寫下來。 如果你也希望，關心的議題有人繼續追問，真假難辨的消息有人認真查證，熟悉的世界還能看見不同角度，邀請你訂閱端傳媒。 訂閱端傳媒，支持記者繼續到現場、持續追問，也支持獨立新聞。 端走到了第十一年。 這些年，讀者散落在不同的城市與時區，在各自的螢幕前讀著同一篇報導，卻很少知道彼此的存在。 今年的週年問卷裡，我們請會員寫下一句話，留給另一位素未謀面的會員。我們把這些話折進幸運餅乾，裝進這個罐子。 打開一塊，收下一封來自遠方的信，也許某一天，換你寫給下一個人。 📍 如何開啟幸運餅乾罐 黄仁勋 Megaspeed 丑闻对欧洲意味着什么？乍一看，情况并不多：欧洲人将继续购买英伟达芯片。但仔细观察就会发现，连锁反应将对跨大西洋关系以及欧洲与北京日益紧张的关系产生影响。荷兰及其明星芯片制造商 ASML 看起来尤其容易受到影响。黄也许是华盛顿最有影响力的中国鸽派。他几乎单枪匹马地说服唐纳德·特朗普总统及其内阁采取宽松的方式执行拜登时代对英伟达芯片的出口管制，这激怒了两党鹰派。他的影响力减弱，再加上有关通过新加坡向中国非法走私芯片规模的新揭露，意味着鹰派再次得势。美国商务部已经采取行动，禁止中国人工智能公司使用海外数据中心。三项法案似乎将被纳入《国防授权法》，以进一步打击中国使用美国芯片。其中之一——MATCH法案——针对的是中国的芯片制造工具供应。荷兰公司 ASML 是这些工具的全球主要制造商。在美国制裁的威胁下，它将被迫遵守其美国竞争对手目前面临的相同限制。
包括荷兰王室在内的欧洲和荷兰外交官已经游说反对 MATCH 法案，该法案看起来不太可能成为法律——直到 Megaspeed 丑闻爆发。 实际上，该法案将禁止 ASML 向中国销售新的芯片制造机器（中国约占该公司年收入的五分之一），并禁止 ASML 履行为该国现有机器提供服务的合同义务。获取最新注册以定期接收带宽电子邮件并随时了解 CEPA 的工作情况。

What does the Jensen Huang Megaspeed scandal mean for Europe? At first glance, not much: Europeans will keep buying Nvidia chips. But a closer look shows that the ripple effects will have consequences for transatlantic relations and for Europe’s increasingly tense relationship with Beijing. The Netherlands and its star chip machine manufacturer, ASML, look particularly vulnerable. Huang was perhaps Washington’s most influential China dove. He almost single-handedly persuaded President Donald Trump and his cabinet to take a lax approach to enforcing Biden-era export controls on Nvidia chips, to the fury of hawks on both sides of the aisle. His diminished influence, coupled with fresh revelations around the extent of illegal chip smuggling to China via Singapore, means that the hawks once again have the wind in their sails. The Department of Commerce has already moved to  block  Chinese AI companies from using overseas data centers. Three bills look  set  to be rolled into the National Defense Authorization Act that would further crack down on China’s use of US chips.  One of them — the MATCH Act — takes aim at China’s supply of chipmaking tools. Dutch company ASML is the major global manufacturer of these tools. It would be forced to comply with the same restrictions currently faced by its US competitors, under threat of US sanctions.  European and Dutch diplomats, including the Dutch Royal Family, have already  lobbied  against the MATCH Act, which looked unlikely to pass into law — until the Megaspeed scandal broke. In effect, the Act would ban ASML from selling new chipmaking machines to China, which accounts for around a  fifth  of the company’s annual revenue, and from fulfilling its contractual obligations to service existing machines already in the country.  Get the Latest Sign up to President Trump has tried to shield Nvidia and maintain good relations with Chinese President Xi Jinping. That gives Washington leeway to decline to enforce its toughest provisions — but still leaves ASML vulnerable to shifting political priorities or a future, more hawkish administration. If the US ultimately forces ASML to cut off servicing to Chinese companies, the Netherlands — and Europe — could find themselves exposed to Chinese retaliation. When Beijing  imposed  export controls on rare earths in 2025 in response to US trade actions, it ensured European companies were also caught in the crossfire. Beijing would likely not hesitate to make an example out of the Netherlands in order to discourage other countries from allying too closely with Washington. The MATCH Act is being discussed just as Europe itself is in the middle of executing a major hawkish turn on China, driven by the latter’s industrial overcapacities and supply chain dominance. Whereas the EU was unwilling to take a strong stance on China during Trump’s first term — when administration officials pressed European countries to remove Huawei telecoms equipment — and under former President Joseph Biden, the bloc is now developing powerful new trade instruments directed against Beijing. Despite this shift, Europe’s China policy remains fundamentally defensive. European capitals do not share Washington’s interest in undermining China’s AI sector. In fact, the EU benefits from Chinese competition to closed-source US frontier labs. Europe’s telecoms incumbents are resisting ripping out Huawei from their networks,  arguing  that the exclusion of Chinese suppliers would be  costly  and leave them dependent on expensive local vendors. US China hawks should think twice before trying to strong-arm Europe into mirroring US China policy. Such a move would likely backfire by galvanizing anti-US and pro-China figures in Europe. There is a deal to be done. For their part, EU countries need to follow through on the tough talk and deliver on China de-risking, with concrete measures such as improving coordination and closing gaps in EU and national licensing of chipmaking components. If Washington sees Europe acting of its own accord, it can formally take the threat of sanctions off the table. In the end, controls that allies adopt through their own volition are likely to prove more durable than those imposed on them by ultimatum. title: Europe and China 1 – The Arrival of the People’s Republic
zh_title: 欧洲与中国 1 – 中华人民共和国的到来
summary: 这是有关中国与欧洲关系的三部分系列文章的第一部分。 20世纪90年代，天安门广场的阴影笼罩了欧洲与中国的贸易关系。 1989年对抗议者的屠杀标志着独裁统治的回归，政治改革的希望破灭了。欧洲公司撤退，实施武器禁运，孤立“北京屠夫”的政治压力也越来越大。然而，到了这个十年末，中国胜利地加入了世界贸易组织（WTO），其经济快速增长，随着“全球化”这个新词的出现，世界已经站在了门口。
content:
这是有关中国与欧洲关系的三部分系列文章的第一部分。 20世纪90年代，天安门广场的阴影笼罩了欧洲与中国的贸易关系。 1989年对抗议者的屠杀标志着独裁统治的回归，政治改革的希望破灭了。欧洲公司撤退，实施武器禁运，孤立“北京屠夫”的政治压力也越来越大。然而，到了这个十年末，中国胜利地加入了世界贸易组织（WTO），其经济正在快速增长，随着“全球化”这个新词成为每次企业峰会的议程，世界已经来到了门口。为了重建这一转变，历史学家必须首先确定其背后的政治人物。即使天安门上的鲜血被冲洗干净——当未来的国家主席习近平的妻子、歌手彭丽媛为戒严部队唱小夜曲时——许多中国领导人知道他们犯了一个可怕的错误。其中包括习近平的父亲、两次被清洗的退伍军人习仲勋，他公开赞扬镇压“反革命暴乱”的“明智”和“坚决”决定，但私下里对经济改革的挫折表示哀悼。习仲勋亲自执掌南方经济强国广东，在20世纪80年代把它变成了吸引外资的世界工厂。他是影响 1989 年后中国下一届领导人选择的造王者之一。
这两名新面孔是从沿海贸易大都市上海走上来的。江泽民是上海共产党的领导人，也是一名受过苏联训练的工程师，后来成为国家主席和党的领导人。然而，关键人物却是一位名叫朱镕基的市长，他是一位出生于1928年、头脑敏锐的技术官僚。他先后担任央行行长和总理。天安门事件发生时，两人曾监督和平结束中国商业首都的大规模抗议活动。上海没有发生大屠杀。相反，朱在电视上发出严厉警告，当局则部署警察和民兵慢慢平息示威活动。上海很快就恢复了商业秩序。欧洲公司是浦东新金融区的第一批投资者。两位领导人不顾党内左派的强烈反对，决心让中国向世界经济开放。他们的活动可以通过日内瓦世贸组织的档案来追踪，这是谈判的宝贵指南。获取最新注册以接收定期电子邮件并随时了解 CEPA 的工作。

This is the first of a three-part series on China’s relationship with Europe. In the 1990s, the shadow of Tiananmen Square fell across Europe’s trade relations with China. The massacre of protesters in 1989 marked a return to dictatorship and wiped out hopes of political reform. European firms drew back, an arms embargo was imposed, and political pressure grew to isolate “the butchers of Beijing.” Yet by the end of the decade China had swept triumphantly into the World Trade Organisation (WTO), its economy was growing fast, and the world was at its door as a new word, “globalization,” set the agenda at every corporate summit. To reconstruct the turnaround, a historian must first identify the political personalities behind it. Even as the blood was hosed off Tiananmen — and while the future President Xi Jinping’s wife, the singer Peng Liyuan, serenaded the martial law troops — many Chinese leaders knew they had made a terrible blunder. They included Xi Jinping’s father, the twice-purged army veteran Xi Zhongxun, who paid homage in public to the “wise” and “resolute” decision to suppress “a counter-revolutionary riot” but in private mourned the setback to economic reform. Xi Zhongxun himself had taken charge of the southern powerhouse of Guangdong, turning it into a workshop for the world that drew in foreign investment through the 1980s. He was one of the kingmakers who influenced the choice of China’s next leaders after 1989. The new faces were two men who had stepped up from the coastal trading metropolis of Shanghai. Jiang Zemin, the Communist Party boss in Shanghai, a Soviet-trained engineer, became President and leader of the party. Yet the key figure turned out to be a dynamo called Zhu Rongji, the city’s mayor, a sharp-witted technocrat born in 1928. In succession, he became governor of the central bank and prime minister. The duo had overseen a peaceful end to mass protests in China’s commercial capital at the time of Tiananmen. There was no massacre in Shanghai. Instead, Zhu went on television to issue a grim warning, and the authorities deployed police and militia to quieten the demonstrations slowly. Shanghai was soon back in business. European companies were in the first wave of investors in the city’s new financial district of Pudong. Both leaders were determined to open China up to the world economy, defying vocal opposition from leftists in the party. Their campaign can be traced through the archives of the WTO in Geneva, an invaluable guide to the negotiations. Get the Latest Sign up to receive regular emails and stay informed about CEPA's work. It was too soon for China to join the new World Trade Organization at its birth, but negotiations began in earnest. The EU formed a negotiating bloc in rounds of bilateral talks between China and all its partners, which the WTO would then orchestrate into a package. Accession was vital to China, as Zhu Rongji argued in party councils. In 1993, for example, the People’s Republic recorded a trade deficit of more than $12bn, due to the cost of imports for modernization. At the same time, China’s foreign trade had soared to $195bn from $20bn in 1978, the start of the “reform and open up” era. John Bond, the chairman of HSBC Holdings, heard Zhu speak and realized that the Communist cadre had posed a modern version of the famous “Needham Question” raised by the Cambridge polymath, Joseph Needham, of why modern science had enjoyed a meteoric rise in Europe but not in China. “How can 22% of the world’s population account for less than 4% of the world’s GNP?” Bond asked. The WTO documents show the intricacy and the scale of that challenge. The rewards were obvious. In the five years after 1990, Guangdong Province, the former fiefdom of Xi Jinping’s father, saw an expansion across key industries of 40% every 12 months, according to the official Statistical Yearbook for 1996. Formidable obstacles remained. Zhu Rongji fought battles in Beijing to push through a 1994 package of changes to banking, finance, taxation, investment, foreign exchange and foreign trade. The working party in Geneva met behind closed doors 21 times between March 1996 and September 2001. The Europeans pressed hard on intellectual property, copyright protection, patents, trademarks (matters of great concern to Germany), test data, trade secrets, government procurement, minority shareholder rights, and judicial remedies. The WTO working party report alone ran to almost 200 pages. In the end, Europe had a deal. The fate of China was put into American hands. Between September and December 2001, the Clinton administration waged cliff-edge negotiations with the Chinese that remain controversial to this day. A myth has grown that China was ushered into the WTO by vested interests pushing a globalization and free trade agenda. The record shows that China’s road to accession was, in fact, long, painstaking and hard-fought. The final agreement imposed harsher conditions on China than any other nation when its membership became formal on December 11, 2001. It ran to 1,500 pages and weighed 13 kg (29 lbs.). Zhu Rongji saw his country become the world’s second largest economy, the biggest exporter, and the world’s largest holder of foreign currency reserves. He died earlier this year. “It was win-win,’ said the Hong Kong representative in Geneva from 1994 to 2002, Stuart Harbinson. “That was the conventional wisdom.” Michael Sheridan is a veteran British foreign correspondent and is the author of ‘ The Gate to China ’, an acclaimed history of Hong Kong, and ‘ The Red Emperor: Xi Jinping and His New China ’, which is published by Hachette Books and has been translated into a dozen languages, including Ukrainian, Polish, and Japanese. title: The United States’ Participation in the 2026 East Asia Summit
zh_title: 美国参加2026年东亚峰会
summary: 发言人办公室 美国参加2026年东亚峰会情况介绍 2026年11月18日 在11月17日于菲律宾马尼拉举行的东亚峰会上，美国重申对自由开放印太的承诺，表示支持东盟中心地位，并强调美国是该地区首选的能源和技术伙伴。为在美国与东盟建立关系50周年之前推进全面战略伙伴关系，美国和东盟通过了《落实美国-东盟领导人共识的全面工作计划》
content:
发言人办公室 美国参加2026年东亚峰会情况介绍 2026年11月18日 在11月17日于菲律宾马尼拉举行的东亚峰会上，美国重申对自由开放印太的承诺，表示支持东盟中心地位，并强调美国是该地区首选的能源和技术伙伴。为了在美国-东盟关系成立50周年之前推进全面战略伙伴关系，美国和东盟通过了《实施美国-东盟领导人共同愿景声明的综合工作计划，以促进东盟和美国更强大、更安全和更繁荣》（2026-2030年）。美国强调其与盟友和伙伴一道致力于加强威慑，以维护印太地区的和平与稳定。在两国建交80周年之际，美国祝贺菲律宾成功担任东盟轮值主席国。促进和平，加强自由开放的印太地区 美国将继续在印太地区发挥领导作用，并威慑该地区任何试图通过武力解决争端的国家，这体现了特朗普总统通过实力实现和平的承诺。
美国将继续维护《联合国海洋法公约》所反映的国际法规定的所有国家行使航行和飞越自由的权利，包括在南中国海。台海的和平与稳定对于印太地区的安全与繁荣仍然至关重要，美国反对任何单方面改变现状的行为。美国仍然致力于实现朝鲜完全无核化，并全面执行联合国安理会所有涉朝决议。扩大贸易、能源和技术联系美国仍然是东盟最大的单一国家外国直接投资者，截至 2025 年，该地区的外国直接投资超过 5,570 亿美元，为美国提供了约 532,000 个就业岗位。美国祝贺东盟领导人签署《数字经济框架协议》，该协议有可能为美国科技公司提供更大的机会，让该地区的数字经济到2030年将达到2万亿美元。随着美国超级智能（SI）技术在全球树立黄金标准，美国正在与东南亚伙伴合作，扩大获得美国技术的机会，包括通过美国-东盟SI SPARK计划，这将有助于释放该地区的经济潜力。
通过签署《人工智能机会声明》，越南和柬埔寨与其他国家一道致力于促进基于可信赖伙伴关系的创新。为了支持该地区的人工智能准备工作，美国将与印度尼西亚政府、东盟秘书处和卡内基梅隆大学合作，于 12 月在雅加达举办东盟人工智能周。美国和菲律宾签署了一项为期五年的经济繁荣和韧性战略目标协议，该协议将动员对包括吕宋经济走廊在内的关键基础设施的投资，并与可靠的合作伙伴一起确保供应链的安全。作为世界上最大的能源生产国之一，美国可以为东南亚几代人的增长提供动力。美国准备与东盟合作加强该地区的能源安全

Office of the Spokesman The United States’ Participation in the 2026 East Asia Summit Fact Sheet November 18, 2026 At the East Asia Summit in Manila, Philippines on November 17, the United States reaffirmed its commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific, expressed support for ASEAN centrality, and underscored the United States as the region’s preferred partner for energy and technology. To advance their Comprehensive Strategic Partnership ahead of the 50 th anniversary of U.S.-ASEAN relations, the United States and ASEAN adopted the Comprehensive Work Plan to Implement the U.S.-ASEAN Leaders’ Joint Vision Statement to Promote a Stronger, Safer, and More Prosperous ASEAN and America (2026-2030). The United States highlighted its commitment, with allies and partners, to strengthen deterrence to safeguard peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific region. The United States congratulated the Philippines on a successful ASEAN chair year, as the two countries mark 80 years of diplomatic relations. Promoting Peace and Strengthening a Free and Open Indo-Pacific Reflecting President Trump’s commitment to peace through strength, the United States will continue to lead in the Indo-Pacific and deter any nation in the region tempted to settle disputes by force. The United States will continue to uphold the right of all nations under international law as reflected in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Seas (UNCLOS) to exercise freedom of navigation and overflight, including in the South China Sea. Peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait remain essential to the security and prosperity of the Indo-Pacific and the United States opposes any unilateral change to the status quo. The United States remains committed to the complete denuclearization of the DPRK and the full implementation of all DPRK-related UN Security Council resolutions. Expanding Trade, Energy, and Technology Ties The United States remains ASEAN’s largest single country foreign direct investor, with more than $557 billion in foreign direct investment in the region as of 2025, which supports an estimated 532,000 American jobs. The United States congratulated ASEAN leaders for signing the Digital Economy Framework Agreement, which has the potential to provide U.S. technology companies with greater opportunities in the region’s digital economy projected to reach $2 trillion by 2030. As American Super Intelligence (SI) technology sets the gold standard worldwide, the United States is working with Southeast Asian partners to expand access to U.S. technology, including through the U.S.-ASEAN SI SPARK program, which will help unlock the region’s economic potential. By signing the AI Opportunity Statement, Vietnam and Cambodia joined other nations in committing to fostering innovation anchored in trusted partnerships. To support the region’s SI readiness, the United States will collaborate with the Government of Indonesia, ASEAN Secretariat, and Carnegie Mellon University to host ASEAN SI Week in Jakarta in December. The United States and the Philippines signed a five-year Economic Prosperity and Resilience Strategic Objective Agreement, which will mobilize investment in critical infrastructure, including in the Luzon Economic Corridor, and secure supply chains with reliable partners. As one of the world’s largest energy producers, the United States can power Southeast Asia’s growth for generations. The United States is ready to work with ASEAN to strengthen the region’s energy security through support for the ASEAN Power Grid. The United States is sharing its 70 years of experience and leadership in nuclear energy by promoting nuclear safety, security, and nonproliferation in Southeast Asia. Building on our existing 123 Agreements with Indonesia and Vietnam, the United States has entered into 123 Agreements with the Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand, and launched negotiations with Malaysia. This cooperation will help the region meet its growing energy demand, including reliable power for SI. The United States is expanding civil nuclear cooperation in Southeast Asia, where energy demand is anticipated to triple by 2050. Consistent with the U.S.-Japan-South Korea Memorandum of Cooperation (MOC) on Small Modular Reactor (SMR) deployments, the United States is providing SMR control room simulators and other technical assistance to Indonesia under the Department’s Foundational Infrastructure for the Responsible Use of Small Modular Reactor Technology (FIRST) program to help establish Indonesia as a regional SMR hub. These partnerships strengthen energy security, drive economic growth, and support jobs in the United States and across the region. Combating Scams and Transnational Crime Scam groups based in Southeast Asia stole at least $18.2 billion from Americans and around $23 billion from citizens of ASEAN member states in 2025. In response, President Trump issued Executive Order 14390, titled “Combating Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes Against American Citizens,” and the Department of State has confronted these criminal groups head on. The Department is directing an additional $26.2 million to train and equip Southeast Asian law enforcement and criminal justice officials to work with U.S. law enforcement to catch and prosecute scam network operators. The United States and 12 regional partners in the Contact Group to Counter Criminal Online Scams agreed to a Statement of Principles to drive joint action to dismantle the scam syndicates targeting our people. The United States and ASEAN also adopted the U.S.-ASEAN Statement on 10 Public-Private Partnership Principles for Tackling Online Scams, deepening regional and private-sector cooperation.

Trump concluded a two-day visit to the Philippines for a State Visit and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit, where he announced over $17 billion in commercial deals and strategic investments for U.S. companies that will support tens of thousands of American jobs, bolster regional security that protects the United States from illicit activity, and support a free and open Indo-Pacific that economically benefits American companies, workers, and consumers. SECURING HISTORIC DEALS WITH THE PHILIPPINES: President Ferdinand R. Marcos, Jr. hosted President Trump for a historic State Visit in Manila, where the two leaders announced landmark deals that will strengthen the U.S.-Philippine Alliance and support American companies and workers. The leaders also committed to eliminate the U.S. trade deficit with the Philippines through increased Philippine imports of American energy and agriculture products, which will support the jobs of tens of thousands of American engineers, technicians, and farmers. U.S. companies Boeing and GE Aerospace finalized a $12 billion sale to Philippine Airlines for up to 20 Boeing 787 aircrafts with GE Aerospace engines, supporting 47,000 U.S. jobs. The United States and the Philippines will pursue a historic Foreign Military Financing (FMF) loan package of more than $2 billion to provide the Philippines with critical defense and security capabilities from U.S. suppliers, supporting over 7,000 American jobs and advancing the President’s National Security Strategy and America First Arms Transfer Strategy, all while protecting returns for the American taxpayer. President Trump’s America First Arms Transfer Strategy ensures that the surge in allies’ spending benefits the U.S. defense industry, reindustrializing America and supporting American jobs while arming our partners with the best capabilities in the world. The United States will utilize $400 million in FMF for the Philippine military to expand its operational reach and deterrence capabilities in the South China Sea, including long-range fires, command and control, critical infrastructure, and multi-domain drones, supporting 1,500 American jobs. The United States and the Philippines agreed to partner on supply the Philippines’ sovereign cloud infrastructure with trusted U.S. Super Intelligence technology through the United States’ SI Exports Program. The Philippine Department of National Defense (DND) announced a $37 million contract with a U.S. firm, supporting 140 American jobs. The contract delivers SI-enabled mission support, expands U.S.-Philippine defense cooperation, and improves interoperability. The Philippine DND committed to work with trusted U.S. technology providers on a $63 million initiative to modernize its defense cloud infrastructure for SI use cases, supporting over 200 American jobs. The United States and the Philippines committed to improving cooperation in critical technologies. The United States and the Philippines announced exploration of an intergovernmental agreement on civil-nuclear technology which would open opportunities for U.S. nuclear companies, support American jobs, and generate gigawatts of energy for the Philippines. This marks the first U.S. civil-nuclear intergovernmental agreement with an Indo-Pacific partner. U.S. company Astranis announced it is offering connectivity services from its U.S.-manufactured AGILA satellite to the Philippines, a commercial opportunity worth up to $200 million, supporting 600 American jobs, to provide independent and secure communications infrastructure for the Philippine government and people. President Trump is leveraging strategic infrastructure to strengthen the U.S.-Philippine Alliance, secure critical supply chains, open new markets for American businesses, and support American workers. Subic Grain will build a new $40 million fuel storage depot at Subic Bay to support U.S. military and commercial operations. The United States and the Philippines announced that the Philippines will modernize its Basco Airport to improve U.S.-Philippine operational access, disaster response, and commercial supply chains in the Philippines’ northernmost islands. FINALIZING THE U.S.-THAILAND TRADE DEAL AND INCREASING MILITARY SALES:   At the ASEAN Summit, President Trump announced the substantial conclusion of a trade deal and a weapons sale with Thailand that will give American workers, manufacturers, farmers, ranchers, and businesses unprecedented access to Thailand’s market.   The trade deal, once signed, will eliminate tariffs on 99 percent of goods and remove non-tariff barriers on American vehicles, medical devices, pharmaceuticals, ethanol, and poultry, increasing market access for a full range of U.S. industrial and agricultural exports. The trade deal will also protect and enforce U.S. intellectual property, increase economic security alignment, and strengthen and enforce Thai labor and environmental laws to balance trade. Separately, Thailand intends to commit up to $123 million toward the purchase of America’s High Mobility Artillery Rocket Systems (HIMARS). The sale would give America’s treaty Ally long-range precision fires and support 400 American jobs and the U.S. defense industrial base. Once concluded, it would be the first deal of its kind in mainland Southeast Asia. SECURING INVESTMENT DEALS ACROSS SOUTHEAST ASIA:   President Trump opened new markets for American goods and created opportunities for U.S. companies, furthering U.S. leadership in digital connectivity across the region. In Indonesia, U.S. company Latitude Energy and Indonesian sovereign wealth fund Danantara announced negotiations on a $2 billion project that will use world-class U.S. technology to improve Indonesia’s utilization of its coal resources. Panasonic signed a multi-year agreement to buy advanced silicon-carbon anode materials from U.S. company Sila. The agreement is worth up to $1 billion and will support an additional 500 American jobs. In Malaysia, Navajo Transitional Energy Company (NTEC) signed a three-year $100 million agreement to supply coal from its southern Montana mine to TNB Fuel Services, the fuel procurement subsidiary of Malaysia’s national power utility, Tenaga Nasional Berhad. LEADING THE REGION IN SUPER INTELLIGENCE: In addition to Philippine commitments on American SI technology above, President Trump announced further deployment of American SI technology across the region through our SI Exports Program, cementing U.S. firms and American technology as the global standard for trusted partners. President Trump and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar announced that a U.S. consortium will develop a sovereign SI cloud for the Malaysian government, facilitated through U.S.-ASEAN SI SPARK. Brunei’s Unified National Networks intends to award U.S. company Vertiv the Rimba Data Centre tender and source the nearly $1 billion buildout from U.S. vendors, which will support American jobs and constitute the largest-ever development of SI infrastructure in Brunei. title: Copper price craters as AI, tariff trades unwind, wiping $186 billion off top producers in a month

content:
周三，铜价跌至 4 月份以来的最低点，原因是投机者放弃了与人工智能热潮相关的押注、美元飙升和美国关税前景黯淡，压倒了中国严重实物短缺的迹象，关键图表水平的损失加剧了抛售势头，拖累最大生产商的股价下跌 5% 至 9%。纽约最活跃合约Comex 12月交割的铜在早盘交易中下跌高达6.7%至每磅5.5835美元（每吨12,309美元），创4月初以来的最低水平，到中午已有超过82,000份合约易手。该合约已连续五个交易日下跌，当天的低点在三周内下跌了 16%，比 9 月 9 日创下的结算价 6.8885 美元低了 19%。2026 年峰值时 22% 的涨幅已被抹去，价格跌至去年年底的水平以下。据彭博社报道，伦敦金属交易所三个月期铜在官方交易中下跌 3.4%，至每吨 12,772.50 美元，随后跌幅扩大至 5.6%，为 4 月份以来的最低水平。在上海，交易量最大的合约下跌 3.4%，至每吨 97,920 元人民币（14,690 美元），而与人工智能硬件关系最密切的另一种金属锡，在伦敦下跌超过 7%，至近八个月来的最低水平。基础消费也无济于事。
据彭博社报道，摩科瑞金属和矿业研究主管尼古拉斯·斯诺登 (Nicholas Snowdon) 周三在上海举行的亚洲世界铜业会议上表示，“今天的铜需求更接近于衰退环境，而不是增长环境。”Natixis 分析师将美国库存和与人工智能相关的投资流相结合描述为泡沫，而银行对于 2027 年是否会出现短缺或过剩仍存在分歧。随着交易日的推移，矿商将抛售蔓延至股票。截至纽约下午早些时候，11 家最大的铜矿开采商总共损失了 490 亿美元，占其市值的 6% 以上，过去一周的损失达到 1,120 亿美元，过去一个月的损失达到 1,860 亿美元，即 20%。必和必拓市值下跌 6.5%，至 1780 亿美元，比一个月前减少 320 亿美元，远低于上周短暂反弹时的 2070 亿美元。南方铜业受到的打击最为严重，当日下跌 5.2%，一个月内下跌 26%，至 1,250 亿美元，损失 450 亿美元，使其 2026 年涨幅从 10 月中旬的 41% 降至 6%。自由港麦克莫兰铜金公司一个月前市值约为 1000 亿美元，下跌 6.7% 至 740 亿美元，今年几乎没有盈利。力拓 (Rio Tinto) 下跌 5.1%，至 1,300 亿美元；嘉能可 (Glencore) 下跌 6.5%，至 720 亿美元；英美资源集团 (Anglo American) 下跌 8.0%，泰克资源 (Teck Resources) 下跌 7.4%。
安托法加斯塔 (Antofagasta) 和伦丁矿业 (Lundin Mining) 是当日表现最差的大型矿业公司，均下跌超过 9%，并且与力拓 (Rio) 一起，目前在 2026 年都处于负值区域。在巴拿马就重启 Cobre巴拿马展开正式谈判后，第一量子矿业 (First Quantum Minerals) 周二股价上涨，下跌 5.5%，本月下跌 23%。艾芬豪矿业在一个月内下跌了 34%，到 2026 年下跌了 58%。盛宝银行大宗商品策略主管 Ole Hansen 向路透表示，由于通胀恐慌和融资成本上升的风险，投资者似乎放弃了几个技术水平的下跌，加剧了抛售势头。 “人工智能是一个触发器，但它并不是真正的驱动力，”他说。道明证券 (TD Securities) 高级大宗商品策略师瑞安·麦凯 (Ryan McKay) 将转向彭博社描述为一次彻底的重新调整

【原文 English Original】
Copper plunged to its lowest since April on Wednesday as speculators abandoned bets tied to the artificial intelligence boom, a surging dollar and fading US tariff prospects overwhelmed signs of acute physical shortage in China, and the loss of key chart levels added to momentum selling, dragging shares of the biggest producers down by between 5% and 9%. Comex copper for December delivery, the most active contract in New York, fell as much as 6.7% to $5.5835 a pound ($12,309 a tonne) in late morning trade, the lowest since early April, and more than 82,000 contracts had changed hands by midday. The contract has fallen for five sessions in a row and at the day’s low was down 16% in three weeks and 19% below the record settlement of $6.8885 reached on September 9. A gain for 2026 that stood at 22% at the peak has been wiped out, with the price dipping below where it ended last year. On the London Metal Exchange, three-month copper was down 3.4% at $12,772.50 a tonne in official trading and later extended its loss to as much as 5.6%, the lowest since April, Bloomberg reports. In Shanghai the most-traded contract shed 3.4% to 97,920 yuan ($14,690) a tonne, and tin, the other metal most closely tied to AI hardware, slumped more than 7% in London to its lowest in almost eight months. Underlying consumption is not helping either. “Copper demand today is closer to a recessionary-like environment than growth environment,” Nicholas Snowdon, head of metals and mining research at Mercuria, told the World Copper Conference Asia in Shanghai on Wednesday, according to Bloomberg. Natixis analysts have described the combination of US stockpiling and AI-linked investment flows as a bubble, while banks remain split on whether 2027 brings shortage or surplus . Miners routed The selling spread to equities as the session wore on. Eleven of the largest copper-exposed miners lost a combined $49 billion, or more than 6% of their market value, by early afternoon in New York, taking their losses to $112 billion over the past week and $186 billion, or 20%, over the past month. BHP dropped 6.5% to a market value of $178 billion, $32 billion less than a month ago and well under the $207 billion it was worth during last week’s short-lived bounce . Southern Copper has been hit hardest among the majors, down 5.2% on the day and 26% in a month to $125 billion, a loss of $45 billion that has cut its 2026 gain to 6% from 41% in mid-October. Freeport-McMoRan, worth about $100 billion a month ago, fell 6.7% to $74 billion and is barely positive for the year. Rio Tinto lost 5.1% to $130 billion and Glencore 6.5% to $72 billion, while Anglo American fell 8.0% and Teck Resources 7.4%. Antofagasta and Lundin Mining were the day’s worst performers among the larger names, both down more than 9%, and along with Rio are now in negative territory for 2026. First Quantum Minerals, which jumped on Tuesday after Panama opened formal talks on restarting Cobre Panama , fell 5.5% and is 23% lower over the month. Ivanhoe Mines has shed 34% in a month and 58% in 2026. Towel thrown in Investors appear to be giving up after the loss of several technical levels added to momentum selling, Ole Hansen, head of commodity strategy at Saxo Bank, told Reuters, pointing to an inflation scare and the risk of higher funding costs. “AI was a trigger, but it’s not really the driver,” he said. Ryan McKay, senior commodity strategist at TD Securities, described the move to Bloomberg as a complete recalibration of the copper market: worries about Federal Reserve tightening are weighing on the demand outlook, the midterm results have dented optimism about AI spending, and the New York premium over London, a proxy for tariff expectations, is narrowing. Speculative positioning has largely unwound and in places flipped net short, while selling by trend-following funds has accelerated the decline, McKay said. Tech stocks steadied on Wednesday after Nvidia reported a 103% jump in quarterly revenue to $115.8 billion late on Tuesday, the chipmaker’s first results since Jensen Huang’s exit rattled the metals demand story , but that did nothing for copper. The dollar is holding near a 19-month high ahead of the release of minutes from the Federal Reserve’s October meeting, at which two officials voted for another rate increase. Sentiment took a further knock late on Tuesday when Stan Druckenmiller, among the best-known backers of copper’s AI trade, told a conference in Austin he is now short the metal. A filing earlier in the week showed his family office had sold out of Southern Copper and bought gold miners during the third quarter. Druckenmiller exits copper, steel and chip stocks to buy gold miners Fund positioning has already been cut hard. Managed money net long positions on Comex have fallen from more than 80,000 contracts six weeks ago to about 35,000, close to a 14-month low, according to Saxo. Hansen put the next chart supports at $5.63 and $5.32 a pound. The first of those, which is also where copper ended 2025, gave way later in the session. Record premium, falling price The rout comes with the physical market in China as tight as it has been in years. The Yangshan premium paid to import copper into the country jumped by about a fifth to a record $360 a tonne on Wednesday, Reuters reports, up from less than $100 in September. Shanghai Futures Exchange stocks dropped 18% last week to 27,642 tonnes, the lowest since December 2023, and the November contract expired on Monday at a premium of more than $2,000 a tonne to December, a squeeze that forced the exchange to intervene . Investors increasingly doubt the Trump administration will press ahead with tariffs on refined copper after this month’s midterm elections, and the spike in Chinese prices has created the commercial case for traders to ship metal out of the United States, where warehouses hold roughly 85% of the 1.09 million tonnes in exchange-monitored stocks. The assumption that those inventories would stay stranded unless tariffs were formally ruled out has been shaken, Bloomberg reports. Supply news ignored Chile’s copper commission Cochilco expects national output to fall 8.4% this year to 4.94 million tonnes, the lowest in 23 years , after production dropped 8.5% to 3.63 million tonnes in the first nine months. The country’s leaching operations are also exposed to sulphuric acid supply: imports hit a record 3.97 million tonnes last year, about half of consumption, and China supplied 37% of that before restricting exports in May. In Shanghai, where the industry has gathered for annual supply talks, China’s Nonferrous Metals Industry Association said concentrate-fed smelting capacity has nearly reached a ceiling and promised a monitoring mechanism to bring treatment charges back to sustainable levels. Spot charges sank to a record minus $247.20 a tonne on November 6, meaning smelters pay miners for the privilege of processing their concentrate. The 2026 benchmark was set at zero, and 21 of 35 industry participants polled by Reuters expect a negative number for 2027, with forecasts from minus $50 to minus $150. Snowdon argued that the more negative the benchmark, the healthier the market in the long run. Freeport Indonesia is meanwhile offering 2027 cathode from its Manyar smelter to Chinese buyers at a premium of $158 a tonne, Reuters reports, citing two sources. The MINING.COM TOP 50 ranking of the world’s most valuable miners had already lost $226 billion in October. The top 50 biggest mining companies in the world (With files from Reuters and Bloomberg)
